claim: Bischl et al. 2023's 43-page landmark HPO survey (836 citations, titled with 'open challenges'), which cites Moosbauer et al. 2022 as related work, contains zero mentions of factorial design, ANOVA, fANOVA, eta-squared, two-way, or OFAT/one-factor-at-a-time anywhere in its text, and does not identify a crossed surrogate x optimizer factorial as an open challenge.
stance_target: Whether the highest-cited forward citer of Moosbauer 2022 extends or kills N6
scope_conditions: Full 43-page survey text, WIREs Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery 13(2), 2023
quoted_support: "It was for example used by Moosbauer et al. (2022) to create a new HPO algorithm by optimizing over the space of various algorithm components. Their analysis showed that an alternative, simpler approach to scheduling multi-fidelity evaluations performed as well as the approach used by [BOHB]" -- cited only as related-work summary, not extended.

claim: Bischl et al. 2023 use the term 'offline' exclusively in the algorithm-selection/algorithm-configuration sense (a configuration fixed for all future problem instances, or a meta-learning model trained offline on empirical meta-data) -- neither usage matches offline model-based optimization as scoped by the audited paper.
stance_target: Domain-boundary clarification for N6's offline-MBO scope
scope_conditions: Section 7.2 Algorithm selection and traditional meta-learning
quoted_support: "In the related problem of algorithm selection (Rice, 1976), we usually train a meta-learning model offline to select an optimal element from a finite set of algorithms or HPCs... This is sometimes called offline configuration for a set of instances, and the obtained configuration is then kept fixed for all future problem instances from the same domain."
